full_name: Scott Manning Stevens | Radcliffe Institute for Advanced Study at Harvard University
bio: Scott Manning Stevens is a citizen of the Akwesasne Mohawk nation and an associate professor and the director of the Native American and Indigenous Studies Program at Syracuse University. His primary research lies in the critical analysis of ethnographic collecting and the significance of material culture collections within a US settler context. Recent published works include an article on the tomahawk as an intercultural object throughout the colonial period of the United States. In that article, he examines the contested and shifting meaning of an object used to represent notions of Native savagery but largely produced and supplied by Euro-American craftsmen.
